report.source_text: A right mini-thoracotomy was performed through the fifth intercostal space with anticipation toward the right lower lobectomy, considering a parenchymal lesion. However, the opening of the chest cavity revealed a tubular, narrow-based pedunculated, mobile, pinkish, cystic smooth lesion arising from the mediastinum around the area of the inferior pulmonary ligament (Fig. 3). There was no adhesion with surrounding structures, and the lesion was completely mobile. The entire lesion was removed just ligating the stalk.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 12-year-old apparently healthy boy presented with occasional mild, diffuse, dull aching, non-radiating right-sided chest pain for a few months. Physical examination revealed no abnormalities. Chest X-ray showed a tubular inhomogeneous opacity in the medial part of the right lower lung field. CECT chest further characterized this as a well-defined, thin-walled cystic lesion measuring 8.5 × 3.6 × 4.5 cm in the right lower lobe with mild marginal enhancement. Right mini-thoracotomy through the fifth intercostal space revealed a tubular, narrow-based pedunculated, mobile, pinkish cystic lesion arising from the mediastinum around the inferior pulmonary ligament. The lesion was completely mobile with no adhesions and was entirely excised by ligating the stalk. Histopathological examination of the excised specimen confirmed the diagnosis of bronchogenic cyst, which was lined by respiratory epithelium with variable amounts of seromucinous glands, cartilage, and smooth muscle.
